subject.title: fix(diagnostic): avoid model-call stream hot-path object copies

question: Should model-call diagnostics intentionally exclude accumulated `partial` snapshots from `responseStreamBytes`, and is eliminating their getter reads worth maintaining the custom serialization fast path now that current main serializes complete chunks?
rationale: Both behaviors are internally coherent, but source inspection cannot determine the intended accounting contract or the minimum performance evidence maintainers require for this added hot-path complexity.

options.title: Rebase and prove the contract
options.body: Require a current-main rebase, explicit byte-accounting expectation, and exact-merge-head measurements showing a meaningful allocation, CPU, or RSS improvement before merge.

options.title: Accept the narrow optimization
options.body: Land the getter-read and snapshot reduction based on byte-equivalence coverage despite the absence of a stable runtime performance improvement.

options.title: Pause the optimization
options.body: Close or defer the PR until profiling identifies this accounting path as a measurable contributor to the broader memory or availability problem.

recommendation.title: Rebase and prove the contract
recommendation.body: Require a current-main rebase, explicit byte-accounting expectation, and exact-merge-head measurements showing a meaningful allocation, CPU, or RSS improvement before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work in the same diagnostic event owner module makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the accounting-contract decision.
